Fork the side worktree from your security lane

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The previously-flagged sentence naming "the evidence-based sharpen" and "the compound step" (old chunk 3) is gone from the body entirely — confirmed by grep, zero hits. Re-derived fresh: chunk 3 line 58's first mention of "the test-strategy skill" and chunk 1 line 15's "Access mapping, STRIDE, and the ADR" both resolve against the enclosing module's `## What You'll Learn` bullets (earn-the-trust.md lines 22-25), which per §1's module-include-order carve-out count as prior context for every exercise the module includes, and this exercise is the module's first include. Chunk 4 line 77's "the quality side waits until you author the test-strategy skill there" resolves against chunk 3's own header + "m3-quality" session name, in-file. "Module 3" (chunk 0) and "the sibling worktree" (chunk 2, from chunk 1) both resolve to earlier same-file mentions. No unresolved referent found in a fresh read.

Only cross-file pointer in body is chunk 1, line 23: "The [Multi-session and Git survival guide](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/multi-session-git.md) carries the longer read." Named by title, not located by page position — matches the §2 navigational-pointer carve-out. No other file named anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw/caught" backward-beat construction anywhere in the body. This exercise is the module's opening item (`## Start here`, first link in earn-the-trust.md), so it has no prior in-module beat to reference. The `**What happened:**` recap block that used to close the file has been cut.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file — this exercise is procedural setup (fork worktree, open second session, arrange windows), no "take a guess" beat present.

Closest candidate is chunk 2 ("Read back the worktree path", lines 44-47), the file's shortest chunk: "Claude reports the sibling worktree path. That path is where the second session opens." Stays inside PASS: it carries one self-standing claim (where the second session opens next), not a bare wait-state fragment.

All four `##` headers are literally true of their chunk content: "Fork the side worktree..." (chunk 1) forks via the prompt block; "Read back the worktree path" (chunk 2) is exactly that beat; "Open the quality lane..." (chunk 3) opens the second session; "Set the two windows side by side" (chunk 4) is the arrangement instruction. None contradicted by chunk body.

Checked all five sub-items against every chunk, including the two new lines (chunk 0's "**The point:** a long-running prompt is dead time only if you have one window" and chunk 4's closer). No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (closest is chunk 0 line 9, "two Claude Code sessions running side by side on one git history" — plain description, not a value claim, stays inside); no number-with-retraction (file has no numeric claims); no abstraction-noun stacks (vocabulary stays concrete: worktree, branch, window, session, skill); no verb-triplet construction present to test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scanned all chunks for repo/authorial vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections). None present. "Lane" (main lane / side-quest lane / quality lane) is this exercise's own defined game vocabulary, self-defined in chunk 1 line 15 ("This is your main lane for Module 3"), not repo-internal maintainer dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 carries four bolded field labels: **Time:**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, and the newly-added **The point:** — each ≤3 words, wrapping only the label not the sentence after it. `grep -rl "^\*\*Time:\*\*" curriculum/exercises/*.md | wc -l` → 37 files; of those, 30 also carry a `^**The point:**` line (verified by loop over the 37-file set) — this is a corpus-wide structural field-label convention identical in kind to Time:/What you do:/What you build:, not a narrative bolded sentence lead. The maintainer block's own Emphasis note (raw source, below cut) is stale — it still lists the now-cut "What happened:" and omits the added "The point:" — but that is maintainer bookkeeping drift, not a body defect the reader hits; the body's actual bold usage stays inside the chrome-label pattern the note was trying to describe. No other bold anywhere in the body (Session/Prompt widget labels are the only other bolded spans, both chrome).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked earn-the-trust.md (the enclosing module): the exercise is included via a plain standalone-paragraph link "[Exercise: Open the side quest](exercises/open-the-side-quest.md)" under `## Start here` (module line 33) — the ordinary include shape that reaches `.phase--exercise` wrapping and the composed deck. Not a phase-less prose section or a dropped supplementary/reference page.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js` and grepped output for "side-quest" → no lines. Headers are imperative labels ("Fork...", "Read back...", "Open...", "Set..."), not `## Phase N:` / `## N.` step headers, so this rule's numbered-step scheme doesn't apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md` → output: "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Manual scan for below/above/further down/at the top/see below across the body confirms no hits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single in-body link (chunk 1 line 23, multi-session-git reference) is named by title, not located by page position — satisfies the surviving requirement independent of the settled mechanism question. This rule is a review surface, never a gate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md` → "files: 1  slides: 4  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets" / "oversized: 0" / "✓ every slide is within limits". No accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four body headers are imperative ("Fork the side worktree from your security lane", "Read back the worktree path", "Open the quality lane in the new worktree", "Set the two windows side by side") — correct mood for an exercise file; no declarative-claim heading present.
